No Balochistan province heading is present anywhere in the fetched OCR text; entries NA-197 (Quetta-cum-Chagai) through NA-207 (Turbat-cum-Panjgur) are inferred to be Balochistan from the constituency names and their position immediately after the Sindh run at the end of the general-members list. NWFP heading claims 34 and 34 constituency rows (NA-1..NA-34) are present and accounted for — counts match. NA-19 Bannu-I has a constituency row printed in the source with no member name in the Name column (blank cell); recorded here with name=null rather than invented or skipped.

Non-Muslim members: heading says TOTAL-09 and exactly 9 names are listed (208-216) — counts match. The source table has separate Community and Remarks(office) columns; per instructions the Community string was placed in the remarks field, and where an office was also printed in the Remarks column it was appended after the community, separated by '; ' (only entries for Lt. Col. W. Herbert Baluch and Seth Chiman Das have an office). Community for entry 215 was printed 'Hindh/Scheduled Castes' in the OCR (garbled 'Hindh') and was normalized to 'Hindu/Scheduled Castes' to match the spelling used for the other three Hindu/Scheduled Castes entries in the same list — a judgment call, flagged here rather than silently made. Entry 211's name was printed 'Em m anul Zafar'; the internal spacing was collapsed per the OCR-cleanup rule to 'Emmanul Zafar' as printed — this may be a garbled rendering of 'Emmanuel Zafar' but was not 'corrected' since the instructions prohibit inventing/correcting names.

Women members: overall heading 'WOMEN MEMBERS-21' matches the actual total transcribed (21 names, entries 217-237). However the first sub-heading is printed 'PUNJAB-21' while only 12 names (217-228) are actually listed under it — the '21' in that sub-heading appears to be the overall women's total misattached to the Punjab sub-section by the source document/OCR, not an accurate Punjab-specific count. This mismatch is stated explicitly rather than silently resolved. 'SINDH-04' matches its actual count (4, entries 229-232). 'N.W.F.P-02' matches its actual count (2, entries 233-234). 'BALUCHISTAN-01' heading claims 1 but 2 names are actually listed (235-236) — counts do not match; both are transcribed. 'MINORITY-01' matches its actual count (1, entry 237); province recorded as null for this entry per instructions since 'MINORITY' is not a province.

Some remarks (Remarks/office column) contain apparent OCR-dropped letters rather than stray internal spacing, e.g. NA-1 'Minister of Sate for Industries' (likely 'State') and NA-15 'Minister fo States F.R.K.A. & N.A' (likely 'for'). These were transcribed literally, uncorrected, since the cleanup rule only covers collapsing stray internal spaces in words, not restoring dropped letters.
NA-123 Vehari-III: name is printed unusually as 'Syed Shahid Mehdi, Naseem' (with an internal comma) in the source; transcribed literally as printed.
The address column present in the source PDF for every row was excluded from the output entirely, per instructions.
All 'Moham m ad'/'Haj i'/'I qbal'-style stray-internal-space OCR artifacts throughout names were collapsed to standard spelling (Mohammad, Haji, Iqbal, etc.); no other spelling changes were made.
